name: PandaStack

modes.label: Hosted8-vCPU burstable template; active CPU and resident RAM
modes.note: Engine selects mandatory8 vCPU. CPUutil is fraction of8, not requested4; equal-work scenario needs halving30% to15%. Free CPU sustained quota2, FreeRAM4 cannot satisfy4/8. No self-host or stopped mode auto-ranked.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Plan RAM cap 4 GiB; account CPU/RAM pools 40/10 (0 is unlimited/custom API sentinel); paid TTL is idle timeout, not running lifetime. Volume quota 1 GiB; max 1 volumes. Also: 1 org seat, 60 creates/hour, sustained CPU capped at 2 cores (API max_cpu_quota_cores 2), sandbox deleted 1 h after creation (apps/DBs exempt); credit exhaustion pauses the workspace (402 on create), never bills.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Plan RAM cap 16 GiB; account CPU/RAM pools 400/800 (0 is unlimited/custom API sentinel); paid TTL is idle timeout, not running lifetime. Volume quota 100 GiB; max 10 volumes.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: Plan RAM cap 64 GiB; account CPU/RAM pools 8000/32000 (0 is unlimited/custom API sentinel); paid TTL is idle timeout, not running lifetime. Volume quota 2500 GiB; max 50 volumes.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Plan RAM cap 256 GiB; account CPU/RAM pools 0/0 (0 is unlimited/custom API sentinel); paid TTL is idle timeout, not running lifetime. Volume quota 0 GiB; max 0 volumes.

caveats: Every first-party template is pinned to 8 vCPUs, not selectable 4; RAM is baked per template. Live API lists Team CPU quota 16 and Enterprise 64, but quota does not prove launchable >8 template cores.
Engine bumps 4-vCPU request to mandatory 8 and keeps CPU utilization fraction. Equal absolute CPU work requires adjusting utilization from 30% of 4 to 15% of 8.
Live API Team SAML differs from pricing page Enterprise-only SSO presentation; confirm plan entitlement.
Pricing FAQ says hibernated state storage currently included/free; lifecycle page says hibernated storage costs. Card follows explicit pricing FAQ but treats this as a documented conflict.
Plain pause freezes CPU but retains RAM on the host; RAM billing while merely paused is not clearly specified. Do not equate pause and full hibernation.
Volume pricing says overage beyond quota, but quota docs also describe hard HTTP 429 caps. Confirm how to buy over-quota storage.
Persistent volumes are host-local; readonly multi-attach supported, writable attach exclusive. Cross-host staging is not yet shipped; not an S3-backed globally durable volume.
Annual 17% discount advertised but credit treatment not verified; only monthly plans auto-ranked.
Performance claims are vendor claims, not independent measurements.

Disk (verified 2026-09-28): each template ships a fixed rootfs (base 2 GB, agent 6 GB, claude-agent 8 GB, browser 4 GB; docs/templates/overview) with no separate rootfs charge; included_disk_gib = 2 (base). Extra space comes from persistent volumes: plan quota included (Free 1 GiB, Pro 10 x 10 GiB = 100 GiB, Team 50 x 50 GiB = 2.5 TiB), then $0.15/GiB-month (pricing page, api.pandastack.ai/v1/pricing volume_usd_per_gib_month). The engine charges $0.15 on all disk beyond 2 GiB, so it overstates cost for disk that fits inside the plan's volume quota.

SSH (verified 2026-09-28): 'pandastack sandbox ssh <id>' opens an interactive PTY over WebSocket (docs/sandboxes/terminal); no SSH protocol or SSH keys are documented, so standard ssh/scp/VS Code Remote-SSH clients don't work. ssh = false.

Desktop (verified 2026-09-28): the 8 official templates (base, code-interpreter, agent, claude-agent, browser, 3 postgres) include no desktop/VNC/GUI template; the browser template is headless Chromium. desktop = false (a custom image could add one; unverified).

Hourly create caps per workspace: Free 60, Pro 600, Team 6,000 (Enterprise custom). Each returns HTTP 429 'hourly create limit exceeded'. Forks, restored snapshots and template launches each count as a sandbox. Bursty fan-out beyond 600 creates/h forces Team.

Non-persistent sandboxes are killed at TTL (default 1 h, refreshed by API activity; paid TTL cap Pro 7 d / Team 30 d idle timeout). Only persistent:true sandboxes are hibernated by the 5-min idle sweeper.

fleet.tiers: Free 5, Pro 50, Team 500, Enterprise unlimited/custom. Aggregate CPU/RAM pools additionally apply: Free 40 vCPU/10 GiB, Pro 400/800, Team 8,000/32,000.
fleet.notes: Free quota can be memory-bound well below 5 for larger machines. 10/50 fit Pro, 300 Team, 1,000 Enterprise subject to resources. Hibernation, retained objects and create-rate limits must also be considered.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Hibernation is automatic for persistent sandboxes. The server-side idle sweeper hibernates any persistent: true sandbox that's been idle for 5 minutes. Wake is implicit on the next API request.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: 5 min idle, only for sandboxes with persistent:true. Hibernate 'dumps the sandbox's memory + disk to a snapshot' (memory included, running processes survive). Non-persistent sandboxes are killed at TTL (default 1 h), not snapshotted. Apps/DBs also scale to zero on idle.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures a running sandbox's memory and device state, plus its disk, so you can create a new sandbox from it later with from_snapshot.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included; new sandboxes boot from it (from_snapshot), list/get/delete via API/CLI/SDK. Also fork (disk only, cold boot), fork-tree (memory+disk, 1-16 children, parent keeps running) and warm fork (REST only).

harness_api.quote: run a self-hosted Claude Managed Agents worker
harness_api.note: No PandaStack API to prompt/stream/resume an in-sandbox agent. The 'agent' template preinstalls claude, codex, opencode, amp, grok, gemini, copilot CLIs (agent_harnesses) driven via generic exec. 'pandastack cma' is a first-party worker that launches Anthropic's ant runner in claude-agent sandboxes for Claude Managed Agents, but prompts/events go through Anthropic's sessions API, not PandaStack's. Borderline; judged not a PandaStack harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote: Beyond these, egress is open: there is no outbound allowlist, and guests can reach arbitrary hosts and ports.
egress_allowlist.note: Only fixed platform blocks: VM-to-VM, link-local/metadata, Stratum mining ports (operator-configurable on self-host). The CMA page says 'you decide what the agent can reach' but no hosted control is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: Beyond these, egress is open: there is no outbound allowlist, and guests can reach arbitrary hosts and ports.
egress_http_rules.note: No egress policy layer of any kind on hosted; HTTP-level rules therefore absent.

ingress_rules.quote: The URL itself is the credential: anyone who has it can reach that port, and there is no separate token to revoke.
ingress_rules.note: Every listening port (up to 32) is automatically public at https://{port}-{sandbox-id}.pandastack.ai; the unguessable UUID is the only protection; no auth/IP allowlist/port selection. Apps get custom domains; DBs need TLS+password.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel and root (sshd + sudo in templates); nftables/iptables inside the guest should work. Not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are decrypted only in the deploy worker and written to a 0600 file inside the sandbox that build/runtime source
secret_proxy.note: Secrets (apps) are env vars injected into the VM; 'Secrets are still visible to your own app's process at runtime'. Sandboxes get env vars via exec. No credential-injecting proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: A volume is a named ext4 image that lives on the host independently of any sandbox. Attach it to one or many sandboxes at create-time and mount it inside the guest like any other block device.
volume_attach.note: ext4 virtio-blk, max 64 GiB each, up to 14 per sandbox, attach at create only; host-local (no cross-host staging yet). Quota Free 1 GiB / Pro 100 GiB / Team 2.5 TiB, then $0.15/GiB-month.

volume_shared.quote: Read-only attach is safe across many sandboxes.
volume_shared.note: Read-only multi-attach only. 'Writable attach is exclusive' (not enforced; multi rw corrupts ext4). Same host only.
